papers.title: Qi-Blood Harmony Formula mediates post-MI cardioprotection via FTO-driven dual modulation of energy metabolism and fibrosis: a multi-omics validation.
papers.authors: Xie X, Wang Y, Dong X, Yuan R, Miao Y, Li P et al.
papers.abstract: Myocardial infarction (MI) remains a leading cause of death worldwide. Persistent myocardial fibrosis and dysregulated energy metabolism following MI contribute to adverse cardiac remodeling and are associated with poor clinical prognosis. Currently, no guideline-recommended therapy provides effective long-term intervention simultaneously targeting both of these core pathological mechanisms. The Qi-Blood Harmony Formula (QBHF), a classical Chinese herbal prescription, has demonstrated cardioprotective potential on attenuating fibrosis, preserving mitochondrial integrity, and restoring myocardial ATP levels in MI, yet its underlying mechanisms and therapeutic targets remain unclear. Using an integrated multi-omics approach in a mouse MI model, we showed that QBHF reactivated genes related to energy metabolism while suppressing pro-fibrotic pathways, as revealed by bulk RNA-sequencing. Non-targeted metabolomics further confirmed its efficacy in counteracting metabolic dysregulation. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing revealed that QBHF altered cardiac cellular composition characterized by reducing a major profibrotic fibroblast subpopulation and expanding a metabolically robust cardiomyocyte subset. Integrative multi-omics analysis identified the fat mass and obesity-associated protein (FTO) as a central regulatory hub modulated by QBHF across bulk heart tissue, fibroblasts, and cardiomyocytes. Crucially, heterozygous knockout of FTO in mice abolished QBHF-mediated improvements in cardiac fibrosis, ATP level and heart function. Consistently, FTO knockdown in cardiomyocytes blunted QBHF-induced ATP restoration. Together, these findings demonstrate that QBHF confers post-MI cardioprotection via FTO-driven dual modulation of energy metabolism and fibrosis. Our findings highlight FTO as a promising therapeutic target and provide novel mechanistic insights into traditional Chinese medicine-based interventions for post-MI injury.

papers.title: Integrative transcriptomic, molecular dynamic simulation and in vitro analysis identify Evodiamine as a multi-target therapeutic agent against cisplatin-resistant non-small cell lung cancer.
papers.authors: Patra SK, Rajeshwari R, Barik K, Kumar A, Biswal BK
papers.abstract:
An integrative transcriptomic, computational, and experimental approach was employed to identify molecular determinants of cisplatin resistance in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and to investigate the therapeutic potential of Evodiamine (Evo). Analysis of multiple Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) datasets identified 100 overlapping differentially expressed genes, followed by protein-protein interaction network analysis that prioritized SPP1, GPX3, HBEGF, and KLF2 as key hub genes. Expression analysis demonstrated significantly increased SPP1 and reduced GPX3 and KLF2 expression in NSCLC tissues, while survival analysis revealed an association between elevated SPP1 expression and poor overall survival. Gene Ontology and KEGG enrichment analyses indicated that the identified hub genes were predominantly associated with extracellular matrix organization, ErbB signaling, glutathione metabolism, and apelin signaling. Molecular docking analysis demonstrated favourable binding of Evo to the identified hub proteins, with SPP1, GPX3, HBEGF, and KLF2 showing docking scores of -9.1, -8.9, -8.9, and - 8.5 kcal/mol, respectively. Subsequently, 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations demonstrated stable SPP1-Evo interactions throughout the simulation period. In vitro validation further demonstrated that Evo significantly reduced cell viability (A549: IC50 = 4 ± 0.23 µM, A549CR: IC50 = 2 ± 0.31 µM), clonogenic growth, migration, and invasion in both cisplatin-sensitive and cisplatin-resistant NSCLC (A549, A549CR) cells. Interestingly, Evo showed better sensitivity towards A549CR cells than parental A549. Evo treatment also increased intracellular reactive oxygen species generation, mitochondrial membrane depolarization, DNA damage, and apoptotic cell death. Furthermore, Evo modulated the expression of the identified hub genes in NSCLC cells, supporting their potential involvement in its anticancer activity. Collectively, the integrated bioinformatics, molecular docking, molecular dynamics, and experimental findings identify SPP1, GPX3, HBEGF, and KLF2 as potential molecular regulators associated with cisplatin resistance and demonstrate the multi-target anticancer activity of Evo against cisplatin-sensitive and cisplatin-resistant NSCLC, supporting its potential as a therapeutic candidate for overcoming cisplatin resistance.

papers.title: Warm needle acupuncture at Jiaji points for lumbar disc herniation: A systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
papers.journal: Journal of back and musculoskeletal rehabilitation
papers.authors: Zuo R, Yun J, Lin X, He X, Qiu F
papers.abstract: BackgroundWarm needle acupuncture (WNA) has been widely used in the treatment of lumbar disc herniation (LDH). However, variations in acupoint selection across studies may influence the evaluation of its efficacy. This study aimed to assess the effectiveness of WNA at Jiaji points compared with conventional acupuncture for LDH.MethodsA systematic search was conducted in the Cochrane Library, Web of Science, PubMed, EMBASE, CNKI, Wanfang, and VIP databases from inception to March 17, 2026. Randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing WNA at Jiaji points with conventional acupuncture were included. Primary outcomes were total effective rate, Visual Analog Scale (VAS) score, and Oswestry Disability Index (ODI). Meta-analysis was performed using RevMan 5.4. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses were conducted to explore heterogeneity and assess robustness, and certainty of evidence was evaluated using GRADE.ResultsA total of 27 RCTs involving 2266 participants were included. Meta-analysis showed that WNA significantly improved the total effective rate compared with conventional acupuncture (RR = 1.26, 95% CI: 1.21-1.31, P < 0.00001). In addition, WNA significantly reduced VAS scores (MD = -1.39, 95% CI: -1.72 to -1.06, P < 0.00001) and ODI scores (MD = -5.24, 95% CI: -6.23 to -4.25, P < 0.00001). However, substantial heterogeneity was observed for VAS and ODI, and sensitivity analyses did not fully explain the residual heterogeneity. The certainty of evidence ranged from low to very low.ConclusionsWNA at Jiaji points may improve pain, functional disability, and overall clinical response compared with conventional acupuncture in patients with LDH. However, methodological limitations, substantial heterogeneity, and low to very low certainty of evidence limit confidence in the magnitude of the pooled effects. Further rigorously designed, adequately powered multicenter RCTs are needed.

papers.title: Effectiveness of Traditional Chinese Fitness Methods on Depressive Symptoms and Glycaemic Control in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes and Comorbid Depression: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Taijiquan and Baduanjin.
papers.authors: Tian X, Wei Y, Bo J, Lin K, Shen Y, Liu Y
papers.abstract:
To evaluate the overall effectiveness of traditional Chinese fitness methods (TCFMs)-specifically Taijiquan and Baduanjin-on depressive symptoms and glycaemic control in patients with Type 2 diabetes (T2DM) and comorbid depression.
RCTs evaluating the effectiveness of TCFMs were identified through 10 major English and Chinese databases, including PubMed, EMBASE, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, Web of Science, Wiley Online Library, ProQuest, CBM, CNKI, VIP, and Wanfang Data. Risk of bias was assessed using the revised Cochrane RoB 2 tool, and evidence certainty was graded using GRADE. Meta-analyses were conducted using the DerSimonian-Laird random-effects model. Subgroup analyses were performed by intervention duration, frequency, and sample size.
Eight RCTs of Taijiquan and Baduanjin were included. All studies were conducted in China, and most had small sample sizes. Most had a high risk of bias, mainly due to a lack of blinding of participants and personnel. TCFMs were associated with significant improvements in depressive symptoms (SMD = -1.39, 95% CI [-2.22, -0.57], p = 0.001). Significant improvements were also observed for HbA1c (MD = -0.82, 95% CI [-1.18, -0.45], p < 0.0001) and FPG (MD = -0.70, 95% CI [-0.97, -0.42], p < 0.00001). The effect on 2hPBG remains inconclusive owing to limited studies. Subgroup analyses revealed no significant effect modifiers for depressive symptoms or HbA1c (all interaction p > 0.05). Sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of the primary findings, though heterogeneity decreased substantially after excluding high-risk studies.
This review provides preliminary evidence that TCFMs may confer benefits on mental health and glycaemic regulation in patients with T2DM and comorbid depression. However, given the low certainty of the evidence, high heterogeneity, and methodological limitations, these findings should be interpreted cautiously. The conclusions are preliminary and require confirmation in larger, rigorously designed studies.
The protocol of this systematic review was registered on PROSPERO (CRD420261287519).

papers.title: Evidence Mapping, Certainty Appraisal, and Acupoint Prescription Pattern Mining of Acupuncture for Poststroke Dysphagia: An Overview of Systematic Reviews.
papers.authors: Lan G, Wu M, Zhang J, Li Y, Wang Y, Su Y et al.
papers.abstract:
To characterize the methodological quality, certainty of evidence, primary-study overlap, outcome coverage, and recurrent acupuncture prescription patterns in the existing secondary evidence on acupuncture for poststroke dysphagia (PSD).
Systematic reviews and meta-analyses (SRs/MAs) evaluating acupuncture for PSD were identified. Methodological quality was assessed using A Measurement Tool to Assess Systematic Reviews 2 (AMSTAR 2), certainty of evidence using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach, and primary-study overlap using the corrected covered area (CCA). Evidence mapping summarized outcome coverage and certainty, and prescription pattern mining explored frequently used acupoints and combinations.
Forty-five SRs/MAs were included. Under the original AMSTAR 2 critical-domain configuration, one review was rated moderate, eight low, and 36 critically low. GRADE indicated that most outcome evidence was of low or very low certainty. The CCA was 0.34%, indicating slight overlap of primary studies across reviews. Evidence was concentrated on total effective rate and swallowing-function outcomes, whereas patient-important outcomes, including aspiration/pneumonia, nutritional status, safety, and quality of life, were underrepresented. Frequently used acupoints included Fengchi (GB20), Lianquan (RN23), Jinjin (EX-HN12), and Yuye (EX-HN13), with recurrent combinations reflecting local stimulation and swallowing-related functional regulation.
Current secondary evidence suggests that acupuncture, primarily as an adjunctive intervention, may improve swallowing-related outcomes in PSD, but confidence remains limited by methodological weaknesses and low certainty of evidence. Future studies should improve methodological rigor, standardize clinically important outcomes, and prospectively validate recurrent prescription patterns.

papers.title: LIPUS promotes calcium oscillations to improve lymphatic drainage and alleviates cold-stimulated pain and effusion in osteoarthritis joints.
papers.authors: Yang J, Liu R, Yang X, Li X, Peng X, Han J et al.
papers.abstract:
Osteoarthritis (OA) patients in remission usually experience acute exacerbations of pain and joint swelling following cold stimulation. This represents one of the characteristic clinical presentations of "cold knees". In Traditional Chinese Medicine, this phenomenon correlates with "Cold Bi", reflecting "lingering dampness" and "stagnation of Blood and Qi" in the joints, and is conceptually consistent with dysfunction of synovial lymphatic system (SLS) observed in OA. However, the underlying mechanisms of cold-exacerbated OA and the therapeutic strategies remain poorly explored.
OA mouse models were established by destabilization of the medial meniscus (DMM) surgery. The mice were exposed to cold stimulation at 4 weeks post-surgery to mimic OA patients in remission experiencing acute cold stimulation. Joint pain-related behaviors were assessed using multiple approaches including gait analysis and von Frey test. Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) was used to evaluate joint effusion. Near-infrared indocyanine green (NIR-ICG) imaging and intra-articular injections of Fluorescein isothiocyanate-dextran (FITC-dextran) were employed to assess lymphatic drainage. Furthermore, the effects of temperature decrease and low-intensity pulsed ultrasound (LIPUS) on calcium oscillations and nitric oxide (NO) production by lymphatic endothelial cells (LECs) were investigated using live-cell fluorescence imaging. Additionally, the mechanisms through which LIPUS plays therapeutic roles were also explored using transient receptor potential vanilloid 4 (TRPV4) inhibitor HC-067047.
Acute cold stimulation aggravated gait abnormality and decreased paw withdrawal threshold in DMM-operated mice. Furthermore, weight-bearing asymmetry and total locomotor distance in the open field were also worsened in these mice. The knee joint effusion was significantly aggravated following acute cold stimulation accompanied by impaired synovial lymphatic drainage. Mechanistically, cold stimulation suppressed calcium oscillations of LECs and decreased their NO production, which were efficiently restored by LIPUS. Additionally, LIPUS treatment improved lymphatic drainage of the knee joint and alleviated cold-stimulated exacerbation of OA phenotypes in mice. These therapeutic effects were significantly suppressed under TRPV4 inhibition as well as hindlimb lymphatic vessel ligation.
Dysfunction of lymphatic drainage contributes to cold-stimulated exacerbation of OA phenotypes in mice, which could be alleviated by LIPUS-induced NO production through the TRPV4/Ca2+/eNOS/NO axis. These findings provide novel insights into the mechanisms of "cold knees" and highlight the therapeutic potential of LIPUS in the treatment of pain and joint effusion in OA.The translational potential of this article: Our study suggests that LIPUS ameliorates cold-induced worsening of pain and joint effusion in OA by improving synovial lymphatic drainage. These findings provide preliminary evidence for the translational potential of LIPUS application in skeletal disorders characterized by lymphatic drainage dysfunction.

papers.title: Shexiang Huayu Xingnao Granule Alleviates Intracerebral Hemorrhage via PI3K/AKT-Mediated Neuroinflammation Regulation: Integrated Network Pharmacology and Experimental Validation.
papers.authors: RuKui Y, MingLi W, Chun L, MeiJuan C, Yuan Y
papers.abstract:
Employing network pharmacology prediction combined with experimental validation, this research elucidated the underlying mechanisms of Shexiang Huayu Xingnao granules (SXHY) against intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH).
Potential targets and related signaling pathways of SXHY acting on ICH were predicted through network pharmacology. An autologous blood injection-induced rat ICH model was established, with simvastatin as the positive control drug. The therapeutic effects of SXHY were evaluated using neurological function scores, brain water content, superoxide dismutase (SOD), catalase, malondialdehyde activity, and brain tissue hemorrhage area. Mechanism studies used a lipopolysaccharide-stimulated BV-2 microglial cell model, assessing inflammatory mediator expression profiles and PI3K/AKT pathway modulation through RT-qPCR and Western blot analysis.
Network pharmacology analysis revealed 360 common SXHY-ICH targets, with 10 core targets (including TNF, AKT1, IL-6, and IL-1β) significantly enriched in the PI3K/AKT, AGE-RAGE, and MAPK pathways; molecular docking further demonstrated potent binding of the key component stigmasterol to TNF-α (binding energy: -9.125 kcal/mol) and IL-6 (binding energy: -8.57 kcal/mol). Animal experiments showed within-group improvements in neurological function from day 2 to day 3 post-ICH in SXHY groups. The observed proportions of animals with improved neurological scores were 88.9% (low-dose), 83.3% (high-dose), 70.0% (model), and 62.5% (simvastatin). However, no statistically significant between-group differences were observed at day 3 (p > 0.05). It also reduced brain edema (high dose: 78.0 ± 0.7% vs.
80.5 ± 1.0%, p < 0.01) and significantly decreased hematoma area (high dose: 0.35 ± 0.50 mm2 vs. model: 1.02 ± 0.93 mm2, p < 0.05); meanwhile, it significantly increased SOD activity (high dose: 68.7 ± 11.3 U/mg protein vs. model: 37.3±14.1 U/mg protein, p < 0.01). Cell experiments further confirmed that SXHY mediates anti-inflammatory activity through modulation of PI3K/AKT signaling, including reduced p-PI3K/GAPDH (p < 0.01), downregulation of proinflammatory cytokines TNF-α/IL-6/IL-1β mRNA (p < 0.01), and upregulation of anti-inflammatory cytokine IL-10 mRNA (p < 0.05).
SXHY may alleviate post-ICH brain injury by inhibiting neuroinflammation throu modulation of the PI3K/AKT pathway. The results provide new mechanistic evidence for traditional Chinese medicine interventions against ICH.

papers.title: Advancements in Natural Product-Based Ischemic Stroke Treatment: Mechanisms, Key Compounds, and Drug Delivery Systems.
papers.authors: Yang N, Li M, Wang M, Li X, Dong H, Yao J et al.
papers.abstract: Ischemic stroke (IS) remains the leading global cause of permanent neurological disability and mortality. Narrow therapeutic time windows and elevated hemorrhagic transformation risks restrict conventional clinical interventions, including intravenous thrombolysis and mechanical thrombectomy. Single-target neuroprotective agents fail to sustain long-term neurological functional recovery, resulting in unsatisfactory clinical outcomes. Natural products (NPs) derived from traditional Chinese medicine exert protective effects against cerebral ischemia via multiple pathways. However, their poor blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability, low aqueous solubility, and inadequate in vivo bioavailability greatly hinder clinical translational application. This review systematically summarizes the pathological mechanisms of natural monomers for the treatment of ischemic stroke and four types of brain-targeted nanocarriers over the past decade. We reconstructed the pathological cascades of cerebral ischemia across the acute, subacute, and chronic repair phases, and critically discussed the inherent limitations of the middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) model and existing monomer-based preclinical studies. This work provides systematic structure-activity relationship evidence and insights into nano-delivery strategies for the development of natural product-based anti-stroke therapeutics. We also propose future research directions, such as staged, sequential administration, precise multi-omics intervention, and standardized nanoformulation development, to accelerate the clinical translation of bioactive ingredients derived from traditional Chinese medicine.
papers.title_ko: 천연물 기반 허혈성 뇌졸중 치료의 발전: 기전, 주요 성분, 약물 전달 시스템

summary.question: 천연물 기반 치료가 허혈성 뇌졸중의 병태생리와 약물 전달 한계를 어떻게 보완할 수 있는지 검토한 연구이다.
summary.methods: 최근 10년간의 자연 단일성분 기전과 뇌표적 나노전달체를 체계적으로 정리한 서술적 문헌고찰이다.
summary.results: 천연물은 다중 경로로 허혈성 뇌손상을 완화할 가능성이 있으나 BBB 투과성, 용해도, 생체이용률 한계가 임상 전환의 장애로 정리되었다.
summary.clinical_takeaway: 한약 유래 성분은 허혈성 뇌졸중의 후보군이지만, 근거의 상당 부분이 전임상 및 전달체 최적화 단계에 있어 임상 해석은 신중해야 한다.
summary.limitations: MCAO 모델과 기존 단일성분 전임상 연구의 한계로 인해 임상적 유효성을 직접 추론하기 어렵다.

papers.title: Artemisinin derived from Artemisia annua L. promotes thrombopoiesis via targeting FLT3: a novel strategy for thrombocytopenia management.
papers.authors: Mei X, Liu S, Zhou L, Wang Y, Hu T, Qi X et al.
papers.abstract: Artemisia annua L. (A. annua) has long been documented in traditional Chinese medicine for managing hemorrhagic conditions, attributed to its cooling and hemostatic properties. These historical applications suggest a potential role of A. annua in platelet-related disorders, although its hematopoietic mechanisms remain unclear. To investigate the thrombopoietic activity of A. annua, identify its bioactive constituent, and elucidate the molecular mechanisms underlying its effects on thrombopoiesis. Chemical profiling identified major compounds in A. annua. MK differentiation was assessed in K562, Meg-01 cells, and primary murine haematopoietic stem and progenitor cells (HSPCs). A murine radiation-induced thrombocytopenia (RIT) model was used to evaluate in vivo efficacy. Molecular docking, drug affinity responsive target stability (DARTS), and signaling assays were conducted to explore molecular mechanisms. A. annua promoted MK differentiation, upregulating CD41/CD42b and enhancing polyploidization. Artemisinin was identified as the principal active compound. It promoted MK maturation in vitro and restored platelet counts, MK numbers, and HSPC populations in RIT mice without inducing systemic toxicity. Artemisinin also reduced bone marrow (BM) apoptosis and DNA damage while restoring platelet function. Mechanistically, artemisinin directly bound to FLT3 and activated the FLT3/MAPK pathway, leading to increased phosphorylation of MEK/ERK and upregulation of NF-E2 and TAL1. FLT3 and ERK inhibition abrogated these effects. Artemisinin is a potent thrombopoietic agent that acts via direct activation of FLT3 and its downstream MAPK signaling cascade. The findings identify FLT3 as a novel therapeutic target for thrombocytopenia and support the potential clinical application of artemisinin in radiation-related hematological disorders.
papers.title_ko: 개똥쑥 유래 아르테미시닌이 FLT3를 표적으로 혈소판 생성을 촉진한다: 혈소판감소증 관리의 새로운 전략

summary.question: 개똥쑥 유래 아르테미시닌이 혈소판 생성과 혈소판감소증을 개선할 수 있는지 평가했다.
summary.methods: 세포실험(K562, Meg-01, 마우스 조혈줄기/전구세포)과 방사선 유발 혈소판감소증 마우스 모델에서 분화·효능을 확인하고, 도킹과 DARTS 및 신호전달 분석으로 기전을 탐색했다.
summary.results: 아르테미시닌은 거대핵세포 분화와 혈소판 생성을 촉진하고 혈소판 수와 골수 관련 지표를 회복했으며, FLT3에 결합해 FLT3/MAPK 신호를 활성화했다.
summary.clinical_takeaway: 방사선 관련 혈소판감소증에서 아르테미시닌의 가능성이 제시되었지만, 임상 적용 전에는 사람 대상 유효성과 안전성 검증이 필요하다.
summary.limitations: 동물 및 세포 수준의 연구로 임상적 효과와 안전성을 직접 확정할 수 없다.

papers.title: Exosomes, a potential approach to enhance the therapeutic effects of traditional Chinese medicine.
papers.authors: Huang T, Wang Z, Zhao Y, Fang W
papers.abstract: Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) exerts unique therapeutic effects, while some unfavorable physicochemical properties limit its therapeutic potential. Exosomes are involved in cellular communication and may enhance the efficacy of TCM. The relationship between TCM and exosomes is supported by the connection between exosomes and the theory of "Qi, Xue and Ye" (one of the basic theories of TCM). Also, the functional resemblance between exosomes and Qi, which is less researched. We fill this gap by systematically summarizing exosomes from different sources with therapeutic effects and exploring the mechanisms and implications of exosomes in TCM treatment. TCM and exosomes undergo two-way communication, with TCM affecting exosomes and exosomes loading TCM monomers. The dual roles of exosomes as destructive agents in disease development are also emphasized; current obstacles and future scope of TCM-exosome therapeutic strategies are fully discussed. The objective of this review is to stimulate further investigation and create a new application of TCM.
papers.title_ko: 엑소좀: 전통중의약의 치료 효과를 높일 수 있는 잠재적 접근법

summary.question: 전통중의약(TCM)의 치료 효과를 엑소좀이 어떻게 강화할 수 있는지를 검토한 연구이다.
summary.methods: 전통중의약과 엑소좀의 관계, 기전, 응용 가능성을 체계적으로 정리한 서술적 문헌고찰이다.
summary.results: 엑소좀은 TCM의 효과를 높일 가능성이 있으며, TCM과 엑소좀은 상호작용하면서 치료적 활용 가능성을 보였다고 정리되었다.
summary.clinical_takeaway: 한약 성분과 엑소좀의 결합은 새로운 전달·응용 전략이 될 수 있으나, 아직 근거와 표준화는 충분하지 않다.
summary.limitations: 임상시험 결과가 아니라 문헌고찰이므로 실제 임상 효능과 안전성은 직접 입증되지 않았다.

pico.p: 전통중의약(TCM) 및 관련 치료 접근
pico.i: 엑소좀을 활용한 TCM 전달 또는 TCM과 엑소좀의 상호작용
